acceptance.denominator: 5 of 5 families released and graded, 0 refused, 0 defects. Each family's own ledger is CLOSED and its sentinel gone at HEAD. Per family the grader checks five things: ledger closed, sentinel absent, live CodeSha256 == the built package, the sweep was the scheduled one, and dlq_drain present. This criterion read FAIL for most of this order's life and that was ACCURATE, not a broken grader: etf's `released` was deliberately null -- neither released-and-proven nor refused -- until its 23:30Z sweep actually ran.

determinism.method: Every family is graded on its OWN next scheduled sweep, never an ad-hoc invoke (the order forbids one and CLAUDE.md calls success-of-upstream-only a defect). The sweep is identified by being the ONE invocation in its cron window, with the window's START-line count printed as the denominator, so a second invocation would be visible rather than assumed away.
determinism.observed: schwab 12:15:49.668Z cron(15 12); blackdiamond 13:00:34.194Z cron(0 13); orion 16:00:42.862Z and eclipse 16:00:05.021Z cron(0 16); etf 23:30:14.490Z cron(30 23) -- 1 START line in the 23:00Z-01:1xZ window for etf. Each family's dlq_drain was then read from the SERVED status object, not from the function's own return value.

mutant.description: The order names no mutant. The sharpest negative here is eclipse, which is the only non-zero drain and therefore the only family whose record could not have been produced by a no-op: 12 messages, 12 distinct keys, ONE signature (VendorDriftError on eclipse/portfolios_simple, extra=['defaultTradingEngineId']). A drain that reported 0 everywhere would be indistinguishable from a drain that never ran; eclipse's 12 proves the code path executes and attributes correctly, and the four zeroes are then honest zeroes rather than silence.
mutant.expected: at least one family's drain record non-zero and attributed to its own family
mutant.observed: eclipse drained 12 of 12 with one_signature true; schwab, blackdiamond, orion and etf each drained 0 of 0 with other_family_returned 0 and unattributed 0 -- and every record carries family = its own family, so no family drained another's messages.

surprises: NFRA_OPLGTW-Z-S117: eclipse vendor drift -- the only non-zero drain, 12 messages in ONE signature, VendorDriftError on eclipse/portfolios_simple with extra=['defaultTradingEngineId']. ARMED and not mine to disarm; it is a vendor-side field appearing in a payload the schema does not admit, and it is the evidence that the drain path really runs.

The guard is NOT this criterion -- a drain record is -- and the row exists so that distinction is recorded rather than argued.

NFRA_OPLGTW-Z-S134: step 6's source-map update reached artifact_sha256 for four families but not their pin or date, and etf's entry carried the NEW artifact hash beside the OLD deployed hash, which reads as a deploy that half happened. etf is corrected here; the other four are terminal grades and eclipse's field is a live peer's act, so the issuer rules. Two routes in the row.

declared_exclusions.item: the set-identity guard verdicts on orion and eclipse
declared_exclusions.reason: Both read FAIL on the sweeps this order grades, and that is DECLARED rather than smoothed over: this order's criterion is the per-family DLQ drain record, not the guard. Row Z-S118 carries the guards and they belong to whoever owns that drift, not to this release. Saying the families are 'released and graded' means exactly what AC2's five per-family checks measure, and nothing about those guards.

declared_exclusions.item: the three stale source-map pins (schwab, orion, blackdiamond)
declared_exclusions.reason: Step 6 binds the entry update to each family's live grade, and for these three only artifact_sha256 was brought forward. Their grades are already terminal, so re-opening them is the issuer's call (row Z-S134). CLAUDE.md rule 4 is explicit that this map is not a deployed-vs-built control, so a stale pin misleads a reader without disarming a mechanism -- which is why it survived four closes unnoticed.

It holds OG-ec-2's repo build (GxWRZhTM...) rather than this order's live value (clrUz/ik...). That is a LIVE PEER's in-flight work -- 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~ZS committed 'eclipse converter artifact uploaded and stamped' at 19:21Z today and its row Z-S131 names both hashes -- so the field is not mine to move and was deliberately left alone.
